biomarker_name.evidence_quote: AMY2A and AMY2B, carboxypeptidase CPA1 and the less characterized CUZD1, to be less abundant in the stool of individuals with T1DM; lactotransferrin (LTF) and the lactotransferrin receptor intelectin (ITLN1)
biomarker_name.section: Results — Human protein excretion in T1DM and microbial functions
biomarker_name.notes: Multiple biomarkers identified as differentially abundant in T1DM patients compared to healthy relatives

biomarker_unit.section: Methods — Protein liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry
biomarker_unit.notes: Units inferred from figure labels and methods describing relative abundance calculations

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: four proteins that are preferentially expressed in the exocrine pancreas, α-amylase proteins AMY2A and AMY2B...to be less abundant in the stool of individuals with T1DM; two with higher abundance in the individuals with T1DM, namely lactotransferrin (LTF) and the lactotransferrin receptor intelectin (ITLN1)
biomarker_value.section: Results — Human protein excretion in T1DM and microbial functions
biomarker_value.notes: Directional changes reported for biomarkers between T1DM and healthy individuals; no specific numerical values provided

value: Study cohort: 20 individuals from 4 families with multiple T1DM cases
Sample collection: 53 fecal samples over 2-4 months
T1DM diagnosis: >5 years, controlled by insulin replacement
Family-level effect: stronger than individual factors on microbiome composition
Metagenomic sequencing: 3.9 ± 0.1 Gbp per sample (101 bp paired-end, HiSeq2000)
Metatranscriptomic sequencing: 8.0 ± 1.0 Gbp per sample (150 bp paired-end, HiSeq2500)
Metaproteomic data: 185,000 ± 13,000 peptide mass spectra per sample
43 ± 14% of microorganisms belonged to mOTUs without sequenced isolate genomes
Intra-individual mOTU profiles were stable over time
Samples did not cluster by T1DM status but by family membership
200 binned population-level genomes with >93% completeness reconstructed
Identified 2,400 ± 1,600 microbial and 200 ± 70 human protein groups per sample
Non-human eukaryotic genes: 0.07 ± 0.05% of metagenomic reads, 0.8 ± 1% metatranscriptomic reads, 2.6 ± 3.1% identified proteins
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: The study cohort consisted of 20 individuals from four families of at least two generations presenting at least two cases of T1DM; 53 well-preserved faecal samples collected over a period of two to four months; A total of 8.0 ± 1.0 Gbp of metatranscriptomic sequencing data and 185,000 ± 13,000 peptide mass spectra were obtained
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive metadata describing study design, sample collection, sequencing parameters, and key findings

host_species.evidence_quote: The study cohort consisted of 20 individuals from four families...Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was performed by CG using their proprietary paired-end nanoarray-based sequencing-by-ligation technology
host_species.section: Methods — Study cohort and Anthropometric, nutritional, clinical data
host_species.notes: Host species is human, inferred from context of human familial study with type 1 diabetes mellitus
